description: A doctoral seminar on turning a research idea into a fundable, defensible proposal: framing the question, synthesising literature, writing aims, planning methods and budgets, and surviving review. Candidates draft each section, plan the work in the diagram studio, and take part in mock panels run in the scenario engine.
modelledOn: Przeworski and Salomon, The Art of Writing Proposals
Booth, Colomb and Williams, The Craft of Research
Funder guidance for research grants and the FAIR data principles
outcomes: Frame a research problem as a significant, feasible and original question with a clear contribution.
Synthesise the literature into a gap analysis using a documented and reproducible search strategy.
Write specific aims and testable hypotheses with defined success criteria and contingency plans.
Justify methods, feasibility, timeline and budget in a form a review panel can score.
Critique a peer proposal using funder criteria, respond to critique, and prepare a data management and research ethics plan.

units.title: Framing a fundable research question
topics: From topic to problem: significance, innovation and the contribution statement
Criteria for a good question: feasible, interesting, novel, ethical and relevant
Research paradigms in computing and health: design science, empirical, computational and mixed methods
Stakeholder needs and local relevance: problems that matter for health and biology in Africa
The one-page concept note and the two-minute pitch
The funder landscape: matching an idea to a programme

units.title: Literature synthesis and gap analysis
topics: Search strategy: databases, keywords, Boolean queries and recording the search
Screening and selection: inclusion criteria and PRISMA-style flow diagrams
Critical appraisal of studies: bias, validity and strength of evidence
Synthesis matrices and thematic synthesis
Types of gap and positioning a contribution against prior work
Reference management, paraphrasing and citation practice

units.title: Specific aims and hypotheses
topics: Anatomy of an aims page: problem, gap, objective, approach and impact
Testable hypotheses: null, alternative and falsifiability
Aim hierarchy, independence and contingencies
Expected outcomes, deliverables and success criteria
Revising aims through critique

units.title: Methods, preliminary data and feasibility
topics: Choosing a study design: observational, experimental, computational and simulation
Data sources, sampling and power analysis
Computational methods: baselines, benchmarks, validation and error analysis
Preliminary data and pilot studies as evidence of feasibility
Risks, pitfalls and alternative approaches
Rigour, reproducibility and threats to validity

units.title: Timelines, milestones and budgets
topics: Work breakdown, milestones and the critical path
Budget categories: personnel, equipment, cloud compute, data, travel and indirect costs
Budget justification narrative
Currency, inflation and funder rules in a cedi and dollar budget
Risk register and mitigation plan

units.title: Writing for reviewers
topics: Narrative structure and plain, precise language
Abstracts, lay summaries and titles
Figures and visual abstracts that carry the argument
Reading funder guidelines and compliance checks
Responding to feedback and planning a resubmission

units.title: Mock review panel and peer critique
topics: Reviewer roles and scoring criteria: significance, approach, innovation, investigator and environment
Scoring calibration and the pitfalls of reviewer bias
Writing a constructive written critique
Panel discussion and consensus ranking
Writing a rebuttal and a revised aims page
Preparing for an oral defence of the proposal

units.title: Data management plans and responsible research
topics: Data management plans: types of data, storage, formats, metadata and FAIR sharing
Consent, sensitive health data and data protection requirements
Research integrity: authorship, conflicts of interest and misconduct
Open science, preregistration and community benefit-sharing
Final submission checklist and the oral pitch

schedule.title: From topic to researchable problem
schedule.exercise: Turn a broad interest such as antimicrobial resistance genomics or maternal-health records into three candidate research questions, and test each against the criteria for a good question.

tasks.title: Score five draft research questions against feasibility, novelty, relevance and ethics criteria and keep the strongest with reasons
Draw a problem tree from symptom to root causes for a health informatics topic and mark which cause your question targets
Choose a research paradigm and design family for a case question and defend it against a sceptical reviewer's objections

schedule.title: Relevance, the concept note and funders
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page concept note for your question, record a two-minute pitch, and shortlist three funders with the fit and eligibility rules for each.

tasks.title: Edit a rambling concept note to one page covering problem, gap, approach and impact, and compare it against a scoring rubric
Map the stakeholders of a community health data project, their needs and influence, and show how the question serves them
Match an idea to one of four funding calls in a case, judge eligibility, scope and budget limits, and justify the choice

schedule.title: Searching and screening the literature
schedule.exercise: Write a documented search protocol with databases, query strings and inclusion criteria, run it, and record how many records were found, screened and kept.

tasks.title: Build Boolean query strings for a research question and choose the query that balances recall and precision from sample result counts
Draw a PRISMA-style flow diagram from search and screening counts and check the numbers at every stage reconcile
Appraise four studies in a case for bias and validity, rate the strength of each, and decide how much weight it carries

schedule.title: Synthesis, gaps and citation practice
schedule.exercise: Build a synthesis matrix of twelve papers, write a gap statement of two sentences, and paraphrase two paragraphs correctly with citations.

tasks.title: Identify which of six paraphrased passages are acceptable and which need citation or rewriting, and correct the weak ones
Organise eight papers into a matrix of method, data, finding and limitation and mark the empty cells that reveal a gap
Write a gap statement for a case literature, test it against a reviewer's challenge that it is already solved, and refine it

schedule.title: Specific aims and testable hypotheses
schedule.exercise: Draft a one-page aims section with a hypothesis for each of three aims, success criteria, and a contingency if the first aim fails, then revise it after peer comments.

tasks.title: Turn five vague objectives into testable hypotheses with a null and alternative and a stated measure of success
Draw the dependencies among three aims, show which can proceed if another fails, and add one fallback aim
Revise a flawed aims page in a case after three reviewer comments, and show how each comment changed the text

schedule.title: Study design, data and computational methods
schedule.exercise: Select a study design for your first aim, estimate the sample size or data volume needed, and define baselines and validation for the computational method.

tasks.title: Pick the right study design for four research questions from a menu and give a reason for each choice
Work through a sample size decision for a clinical data study, adjust effect size and power, and see how cost changes
Draw a validation design for a prediction method including baselines, held-out data, external test set and error analysis

schedule.title: Feasibility, risks and rigour
schedule.exercise: Describe the pilot result that proves your approach could work, list the three biggest risks with alternatives, and name four threats to validity with mitigations.

tasks.title: Choose which of four pilot results gives the strongest feasibility argument for a case proposal and justify the choice
Build a risk matrix of likelihood and impact for six project risks and pair each high risk with an alternative approach
Find the threats to validity in a described study, rank them, and recommend design changes that address the worst two

schedule.title: Timeline, milestones and budget
schedule.exercise: Produce a three-year Gantt chart with milestones for your proposal and a costed budget with justification, in cedis and dollars, within a stated funder ceiling.

tasks.title: Build a Gantt chart for a three-year project from a work breakdown list with six milestones and mark the critical path
Assemble a budget across categories under a funder ceiling, cut it when a reviewer reduces funds by 15 percent, and justify what stays
Add a delay to a critical activity in a project network, find the effect on completion, and add a mitigation to the risk register

schedule.title: Writing for reviewers
schedule.exercise: Rewrite your abstract to 250 words and a lay summary of 100 words, add one figure that carries the argument, and run a compliance check against the funder guidelines.

tasks.title: Compare three abstracts for the same project, rate them for clarity and completeness, and write the best final version
Design a single overview figure showing problem, aims, methods and outcomes, and test whether a reader can follow it in one minute
Check a draft proposal against a funder's guidelines in a case, find the compliance failures, and fix the ones that would reject it

schedule.title: Reviewing and scoring proposals
schedule.exercise: Score two anonymised proposals on the funder criteria, write a half-page critique of each with strengths and weaknesses, and compare your scores with those of two peers.

tasks.title: Score a sample proposal on five criteria with the rubric and record one sentence of evidence for each score
Calibrate your scores against three other reviewers on the same proposals and discuss where bias or harshness explains differences
Write a written critique of a proposal that is constructive, specific and actionable, and be judged against a rubric

schedule.title: Panel discussion, rebuttal and oral defence
schedule.exercise: Take part in a mock panel that ranks six proposals, write a one-page rebuttal to your own panel critique, and defend your aims in a ten-minute oral presentation with questions.

tasks.title: Join a mock panel discussion in a scenario and argue for your assigned proposal's ranking using the evidence in your critique
Respond to three critiques of your proposal, deciding which to accept, rebut or partly address, and record revised text
Answer six hostile questions in a simulated oral defence, and be scored on accuracy, honesty about limits and clarity

schedule.title: Data management and sensitive health data
schedule.exercise: Write a two-page data management plan for your project covering data types, storage, metadata, retention and sharing, and describe the consent and protection steps for sensitive patient data.

tasks.title: Complete a data management plan template for a genomic study, choosing formats, repository and access conditions for each dataset
Decide how to obtain consent and protect identifiable data in a case involving rural clinic records, and justify the safeguards
Resolve an authorship dispute and a conflict of interest in a case, citing research integrity principles for each decision

schedule.title: Open science, community benefit and final submission
schedule.exercise: Complete the final submission checklist for your proposal, write a plan for returning findings to the community, and give a five-minute pitch to the class.

tasks.title: Work through a submission checklist for a full proposal, tick each requirement, and fix the three items that are incomplete
Draw a plan showing preregistration, data release and community feedback steps across your project timeline
Design a benefit-sharing plan for a study using community health data and evaluate it against a panel's expectations
